# ForgeaX — full site content

> ForgeaX is an AI-native personal game development studio. Describe the game you want (by chat, in a visual editor, and — soon — with images or video) and AI writes the ECS engine code, hot-reloading live in your browser. Open source under Apache License 2.0. This file is a single-document mirror of the public website for machine consumption.

Site: https://forgeax.github.io · GitHub: https://github.com/ForgeaX-Games · License: Apache-2.0

---

## Home

**Your personal game studio.**

ForgeaX is an AI-native game development studio. Turn your ideas into playable games — AI writes the engine code, hot-reloading live in your browser.

By the numbers: 29 @forgeax engine packages · 4 playable game demos · dual RHI (WebGPU + wasm) · Apache 2.0.

Why ForgeaX — a studio that writes the engine for you:
- **Many ways to create** — chat, a visual editor, and image/video input later; express your ideas whatever way suits you.
- **Agentic by design** — agents plan, design and write the engine code; you set requirements and review.
- **Live hot-reload** — every change lands in the preview instantly; what you say is what you play.
- **Real ECS engine** — a genuine entity-component-system engine with dual-RHI rendering, in a browser studio.
- **Runs in the browser** — WebGPU-powered, web and desktop on one stack, up and running in a minute.
- **Open source** — Apache 2.0; free to fork, use, ship and build commercially with.

---

## About / vision

ForgeaX is an AI-native personal game studio. We believe the barrier to making games is being redefined by AI.

Our vision: **let smaller teams, with AI, make games that used to require much larger ones.** Not to replace creators, but to hand the heavy engineering and production between "idea" and "playable game" to AI.

How it works: In the studio you describe the game you want to an AI lead called Forge — through chat, by working directly in a visual editor, and (later) with inputs like images and video. It plans, brings in specialized sub-agents when needed (gameplay, design, art), then writes the engine code itself, hot-reloading the result into a live browser preview.

Underneath are two in-house foundations: an engine redesigned for the AI's point of view (so AI can read it, write it, and understand its errors), and a development loop that pushes AI to get it right (requirements in, playable output out, every step observable and traceable).

### Why an AI-native engine

Most game-engine APIs are written for humans. When AI becomes the one writing the code, the engine should look different. ForgeaX's stance: **AI is the engine's first user. When "friendly to AI" conflicts with "friendly to humans," AI wins.** Concretely:

1. **One source of truth, derive the rest.** A fact is defined in exactly one place; everything else derives from it. Component fields live inline in a schema — inspectors, debuggers and tooling read the schema instead of grepping source and guessing.
2. **Errors AI can understand and recover from.** A closed set of error codes, each carrying structured "what / why / how to recover" info, so AI knows what to change next.
3. **Structured data instead of "look at the screen".** The engine can capture a frame of render calls — draw calls, bindings, render targets, pipeline state — to read offline, replay, and inspect the full state at the Nth draw. A visual problem becomes data AI can read.
4. **Two implementations that check each other.** The render layer has two backends (WebGPU and a wasm one) behind one interface; they render side by side, so misuse of an API diverges and is caught automatically.

Common yardstick: the fewer concepts a reader (human or AI) must hold in their head, the better.

### How AI gets a feature right

Not by getting it right first try, but with an observable, traceable pipeline: requirements → research → plan → implement → verify → judgment → finalize. An orchestrator drives the state machine; humans inject judgment at two points: stating requirements and reviewing results. Verification has two AI gates (static docs/API review, plus a sandbox that actually runs and screenshots). After each feature, friction is captured as feedback that upgrades the pipeline itself.

Where we are: the current stage is turning ideas into playable games with AI — playable FPS, ARPG, survival and shooter demos exist, with an engine covering PBR rendering, physics and skeletal animation. Longer term we also watch: AI and humans co-designing games, interoperating with the open-source ecosystem, and how AI world-models might evolve what an "engine" is.

Open source: the ForgeaX tool layer is licensed under Apache License 2.0.

> Let smaller teams make bigger games.

---

## Showcase (game demos)

Each demo proves out a slice of the engine and studio; their code, scenes and config were all made in the Studio.

- **Sector Strike** — FPS. An endless arena: 4 weapons, double headshot damage, enemies spawning from the edges, score-chasing. (pointer-lock, first-person, endless)
- **Hellforge** — ARPG (Diablo-ish). A 2.5D top-down dark-fantasy ARPG: a skeletally-animated witch casting Fire Bolt, with idle/walk/run/cast/death transitions, plus XP and loot. (skeletal animation, 2.5D, spells)
- **Cow Survivor** — survival, two levels. Switches between a daytime cow pasture and a night graveyard; 3D physics, validating the multi-level / scene-reuse pipeline.
- **Shoot Opt** — shooter, performance stress test. Built to stress-test the ECS and bulk-entity limits; results drove engine performance gains.

---

## Tutorials

### Have your AI CLI clone & launch ForgeaX
The most AI-native install: hand the repo to your coding-CLI agent (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / forgeax) and let it clone, install, launch, and report the local URL. You need: an AI coding CLI that can run shell commands; git and Bun installed; an AI model API key. Example instruction: "Clone https://github.com/ForgeaX-Games/forgeax-studio (with --recurse-submodules), cd in, run the install script, then the start script, and tell me the local URL." Manual equivalent: `git clone --recurse-submodules <repo>` → `bun fx setup` → `bun fx start`. All operations go through one entry point, `bun fx <command>` (setup / update / start [web|app] / stop / restart / status / doctor / build app); these are cross-platform Bun scripts — the same commands on macOS, Linux and Windows, with no Git-Bash needed on Windows. (Open source under Apache-2.0; latest stable v0.2.0, all repos at https://github.com/ForgeaX-Games.)

### Quick start: your first game
ForgeaX's core workflow is one sentence: describe the game you want to Forge, and let it handle the rest. Launch the studio (chat on the left, live preview on the right). Say a request in plain words (e.g. a top-down game where a character runs, space fires bullets, enemies spawn, hits score). Forge clarifies, plans, and writes the engine code itself; it hot-reloads into the preview. Keep giving feedback to iterate. The loop: describe → generate → play → describe again.

## Documentation (outline)

User-facing guide; chapters are being filled in:
1. Before you start — what ForgeaX is; install & launch; the interface.
2. Core concepts — a "project" is a game; Forge and its sub-agents; what a session is.
3. Build by chatting — describing ideas clearly; watching Forge plan/code/run; iterating.
4. Scenes & editor — preview & workbench; editing scenes with changes flowing back live; organizing levels.
5. Assets — character portraits & turnarounds; 2D/3D animation; 3D models, VFX, UI, music.
6. Run & preview — web and desktop modes; hot-reload; troubleshooting.
7. Publish & share — export your game; share it to play.
8. Advanced — switch/configure the AI backend; write workbench plugins; customize agent personas.

## Engine + SDK setup for AI

The complete machine-readable setup contract is [the Engine + SDK AI guide](https://forgeax.github.io/download/engine-ai.md).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Probe npm before changing files. If `@forgeax/engine-sdk` returns 404, stop and report that the SDK carrier is not published; never guess a version or use a private GitHub Release.

| Surface | Package | Action |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Runtime + CLI | `@forgeax/engine` | Install in an existing ForgeaX game, or invoke with `pnpm dlx` to fetch the SDK. |
| npm SDK carrier | `@forgeax/engine-sdk` | Let `forgeax sdk install` fetch the exact version-matched carrier; it intentionally omits `store/pnpm`, so the generated project installs its locked Engine dependencies from npm. Do not add it as a runtime dependency. |

When both registry versions exist and match, run:

```bash
pnpm dlx @forgeax/engine@<version> sdk install <empty-sdk-dir> --version <version>
<sdk-dir>/bin/forgeax new <game-dir>
```

The game directory must be outside the SDK root. For an existing ForgeaX game (with `forge.json`, `package.json`, and its entry module), install `@forgeax/engine` and run `forgeax init` instead of using SDK `new`.
